questions.q: Which of the following is a cereal crop?
questions.explanation: Wheat is a cereal. Gram is a pulse, and soybean and groundnut are oilseeds.

questions.q: Which of the following is a pulse?
questions.explanation: Lentil (masur) is a pulse. Rice, maize and jowar are cereals.

questions.q: A hoe is a farm tool used for:
options: Removing weeds and loosening the soil
questions.explanation: A hoe is a long rod with a bent, broad, sharp plate that is used to remove weeds and loosen soil.

questions.q: A combine harvester is a machine that:
options: Harvests the crop and also separates the grain from the husk
questions.explanation: A combine harvester cuts the crop, threshes it and separates the grain in one operation.

questions.q: What is irrigation, and why do crops need it?
questions.answer: Irrigation is the supply of water to crops at regular intervals. Plants need water to absorb nutrients from the soil, and water is also needed for germination, growth and to protect crops from frost and hot air currents.
keyPoints: Supply of water to crops at intervals
questions.explanation: The timing and amount of irrigation differ for each crop.

questions.q: If the same crop is grown in the same field year after year, the soil becomes poor because:
options: The same crop takes up the same nutrients from the soil again and again
questions.explanation: Repeatedly growing one crop depletes particular nutrients, so farmers rotate different crops.

questions.q: A farmer is about to spray a weedicide in the field. Which precaution is most important?
options: Wear a protective cover over the mouth and nose, and wash hands afterwards
Spray when the wind blows toward him
Taste the liquid to check strength
Spray without any cover to save time
questions.explanation: Weedicides are poisonous chemicals, so the farmer must protect his skin and lungs.

questions.q: Why is the soil ploughed and broken into fine pieces before sowing? How do earthworms help?
questions.answer: Loose soil lets the roots go deep, gets more air and lets roots breathe, and brings nutrient-rich soil to the top. Earthworms and microbes in the soil help to turn and mix the soil and add humus, so the soil stays fertile.
keyPoints: Loose soil helps roots penetrate and breathe
Earthworms and microbes turn the soil and add humus
questions.explanation: Soil preparation helps the crop to establish itself.

questions.q: Curd is formed from milk by the action of:
questions.explanation: Lactobacillus bacteria turn milk into curd.

questions.q: Penicillin, the first antibiotic, was discovered by:
questions.explanation: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin from the Penicillium mould.

questions.q: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine against:
questions.explanation: Jenner developed the smallpox vaccine.

questions.q: Which of the following diseases can spread through contaminated drinking water?
questions.explanation: Cholera, typhoid and hepatitis A spread through contaminated water.

questions.q: Explain how curd is made at home from milk.
questions.answer: A little curd, which contains Lactobacillus bacteria, is added to warm milk and left undisturbed for some hours. The bacteria multiply and change the milk into curd.
keyPoints: Add a little curd to warm milk
questions.explanation: The starter curd supplies the bacteria.

questions.q: Why is it advised to boil drinking water in places where the water supply may be unsafe?
questions.explanation: Heat kills most microbes in water that could otherwise cause disease.

questions.q: Food is stored in a refrigerator because:
options: Low temperature slows the growth of microorganisms
The refrigerator kills all microbes inside
questions.explanation: Cold slows down the growth of microorganisms, so food keeps longer.

questions.q: Distinguish between a vaccine and an antibiotic.
questions.answer: A vaccine is given before infection to prepare the body to fight a disease by making antibodies, so it prevents illness. An antibiotic is a medicine given to kill or stop bacteria after a person is infected.
keyPoints: Vaccine prevents disease by making antibodies
questions.explanation: One prevents, the other cures bacterial infections.

questions.q: Fibres obtained from plants and animals, such as cotton, wool and silk, are called:
questions.explanation: Natural fibres come from plant or animal sources.

questions.q: Polythene is commonly used to make:
questions.explanation: Polythene is a light, flexible thermoplastic used for bags and packaging.

questions.q: Which synthetic fibre is prepared by chemical treatment of wood pulp?
questions.explanation: Rayon is made from the cellulose of wood pulp.

questions.q: A polymer is:
options: A small single unit of matter
A large molecule made of many small units joined together
questions.explanation: Polymers are made by joining a large number of small units called monomers.

questions.q: What do biodegradable and non-biodegradable mean? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Biodegradable materials can be broken down by microorganisms into simple substances, for example vegetable waste. Non-biodegradable materials cannot be broken down in this way, for example plastic bags.
questions.explanation: Plastics stay in the environment for a long time.

questions.q: Melamine is used to make kitchenware and fire-resistant fabrics because it:
options: Is a good conductor of heat
Resists heat and does not catch fire easily
questions.explanation: Melamine is a thermosetting plastic that resists fire and heat.

questions.q: Clothes made of synthetic fibres dry faster than cotton clothes because synthetic fibres:
options: Are heated by the Sun more
questions.explanation: Synthetic fibres absorb little water, so they dry quickly.

questions.q: In hot, humid summers, cotton clothes are more comfortable than polyester clothes. Why?
questions.answer: Cotton absorbs sweat and lets it evaporate, which cools the body. Polyester absorbs very little water, so sweat stays on the skin and the person feels hot and sticky.
questions.explanation: Absorbency decides comfort in hot weather.

questions.q: Which of the following non-metals is lustrous (shiny)?
questions.explanation: Iodine is a non-metal with a shining surface. Most non-metals are dull.

questions.q: The property of metals by which they can be beaten into thin sheets is called:
questions.explanation: Malleability is the property of being hammered into thin sheets. Aluminium and silver foil are examples.

questions.q: Solid non-metals such as sulphur are generally:
questions.explanation: Solid non-metals break into pieces when hammered, so they are brittle.

questions.q: Which of the following metals reacts the most vigorously with cold water?
questions.explanation: Sodium reacts violently with water. Copper and gold do not react with it.

questions.q: What is a displacement reaction? Give an example involving a metal.
questions.answer: A displacement reaction is one in which a more reactive metal pushes out a less reactive metal from its salt solution. For example, iron displaces copper from copper sulphate solution.
keyPoints: More reactive metal displaces less reactive metal
From a solution of its salt
Example with iron and copper sulphate
questions.explanation: Reactivity decides which metal is displaced.

questions.q: A dull, grey piece of an old metal object becomes shiny after rubbing with sandpaper. The reason is that:
options: The metal changes into a non-metal
Heat is added to the metal
A dull layer of oxide or tarnish on the surface was rubbed off
questions.explanation: Metals form a dull coat on the surface by reacting with air, and rubbing removes it to show the shiny metal.

questions.q: Aluminium foil is used for wrapping food because it:
options: Can be rolled into very thin sheets and does not readily react with food
questions.explanation: Aluminium is malleable and fairly unreactive, so it is suitable for wrapping food.

questions.q: Name two ways to prevent iron objects from rusting and explain how one of them works.
questions.answer: Rusting can be prevented by painting or by oiling and greasing the iron. These coatings keep air and moisture away from the surface, and iron needs both to rust.
keyPoints: Coating keeps out air and moisture
Rusting needs both oxygen and water
questions.explanation: Rusting is prevented by stopping contact with air and water.

questions.q: LPG stands for:
questions.explanation: LPG, used for cooking, is a petroleum product stored as a liquid under pressure.

questions.q: Coal is mostly made of:
questions.explanation: Coal contains a large amount of carbon.

questions.q: The slow conversion of dead vegetation into coal over millions of years is called:
questions.explanation: Carbonisation is the slow change of buried plant matter into coal.

questions.q: What are fossil fuels? Name two.
questions.answer: Fossil fuels are fuels formed from the remains of dead plants and animals buried under the earth for millions of years. Coal and petroleum are examples.
keyPoints: Formed from dead plants and animals
questions.explanation: Fossil fuels are limited resources.

questions.q: In a petroleum refinery, the different products are separated from crude oil on the basis of their different:
questions.explanation: Heating crude oil makes its parts boil off at different temperatures, so each can be collected separately.

questions.q: Coal and petroleum will not last forever because:
options: They are present only in the sea
The rate at which we use them is much greater than the rate at which they form
questions.explanation: They take millions of years to form but are being consumed quickly.

questions.q: Mention three ways in which a driver can save petrol or diesel.
questions.answer: A driver can switch off the engine at traffic lights, drive at a steady moderate speed and keep the tyres inflated to the correct pressure. Regular servicing of the vehicle also saves fuel.
keyPoints: Switch off engine at red light
questions.explanation: Saving fuel reduces pollution and cost.

questions.q: Which of the following is a feature of an ideal fuel?
options: It is cheap, easily available and burns easily without harmful products
It produces a lot of smoke
It burns only at very high temperatures
questions.explanation: A good fuel should be cheap, easy to get and burn cleanly.

questions.q: Which of the following is a gaseous fuel?
questions.explanation: LPG is a fuel that is a gas at ordinary pressure.

questions.q: In a candle flame, the bright yellow middle zone is due to:
options: Partial burning of the fuel, in which tiny unburnt carbon particles glow
questions.explanation: The middle zone has partial combustion and glowing carbon particles, so it is bright.

questions.q: State the three ways of putting out a fire.
questions.answer: A fire can be put out by cutting off the supply of air (oxygen), removing the fuel, or cooling the fuel below its ignition temperature. For example, water cools the burning material.
questions.explanation: Removing any one of the three requirements stops the fire.

questions.q: Oil in a frying pan catches fire. What is the safest first action?
options: Cover the pan with a lid
questions.explanation: A lid cuts off the air, so the fire goes out. Water would spread burning oil.

questions.q: A gas stove gives more heat than burning the same mass of wood. This is because LPG has:
options: A higher calorific value than wood
questions.explanation: A fuel with a higher calorific value gives more heat per kilogram.

questions.q: How does burning of fuels contribute to global warming?
questions.answer: Burning fuels such as coal, petrol and diesel releases carbon dioxide into the air. Carbon dioxide traps heat in the atmosphere, so increased amounts raise the temperature of the Earth.
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide is a greenhouse gas.

questions.q: A large area set aside to conserve wild animals, plants and their habitat, where private activities such as grazing and cultivation are not allowed, is a:
questions.explanation: National parks are strictly protected areas for wildlife and natural vegetation.

questions.q: Project Tiger was started to:
options: Protect tigers and their habitats in India
questions.explanation: Project Tiger is a conservation programme to protect tigers and the forests in which they live.

questions.q: Which of the following is a cause of extinction of animal species?
questions.explanation: Poaching kills animals for skin, horn or ivory and can wipe out a species.

questions.q: Give two reasons why forests are important.
questions.answer: Forests are home to many plants and animals. They give us wood, medicines and food, prevent soil erosion, and absorb carbon dioxide while releasing oxygen.
questions.explanation: Forests support life and the environment.

questions.q: Why is destruction of habitat a major threat to wild animals?
options: They lose their food, shelter and breeding places
questions.explanation: Animals depend on their habitat for food, water, shelter and breeding.

questions.q: If all the snakes in a field are killed, what is most likely to happen?
options: The number of frogs will not change
The number of rats may increase and damage the crop
questions.explanation: Snakes feed on rats. Without them, rats can multiply and damage grain.

questions.q: Suggest three ways in which students can help to protect forests and wildlife.
questions.answer: Students can plant and take care of trees, avoid wasting paper, and refuse to buy products made from wild animals. They can also spread awareness about not littering or disturbing forests.
keyPoints: Do not buy wildlife products or spread awareness
questions.explanation: Small actions by many people help conservation.

questions.q: Which of the following is found only in plant cells?
questions.explanation: A cell wall is found around plant cells and not animal cells.

questions.q: Cells can be seen with the help of a:
questions.explanation: Most cells are too small to be seen with the naked eye and are studied with a microscope.

questions.q: The genes that pass on features from parents to children are present on the:
questions.explanation: Chromosomes in the nucleus are made of genes.

questions.q: Write the function of the nucleus and the cytoplasm.
questions.answer: The nucleus controls all the activities of the cell and holds the chromosomes. The cytoplasm is the jelly-like part in which the organelles lie and where many chemical reactions of the cell take place.
keyPoints: Nucleus controls the cell and holds chromosomes
questions.explanation: Both are essential parts of every cell.

questions.q: A scientist finds that a cell has a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole. The cell most likely came from:
questions.explanation: Cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole are typical features of plant cells.

questions.q: Which statement about the cell membrane is correct?
options: It is present only in plant cells
It is a thick rigid layer outside every cell
It is present in both plant and animal cells and controls what enters and leaves
questions.explanation: All cells have a cell membrane around the cytoplasm.

questions.q: What is the function of the large vacuole in a plant cell?
questions.answer: The vacuole stores water, food and waste substances. It also keeps the cell firm because it is filled with fluid pressing on the cell wall.
questions.explanation: A large central vacuole is typical of mature plant cells.

questions.q: The change of a tadpole into an adult frog is called:
questions.explanation: Metamorphosis is the change in body form during development.

questions.q: A zygote divides repeatedly and forms a ball of cells called the:
questions.explanation: The zygote divides to form an embryo.

questions.q: Which of the following animals lays eggs (is oviparous)?
questions.explanation: A hen lays eggs, while dogs, cats and cows give birth to young ones.

questions.q: What is the difference between oviparous and viviparous animals? Give one example of each.
questions.answer: Oviparous animals lay eggs, and the young develop outside the mother's body, for example hens. Viviparous animals give birth to young ones that have developed inside the mother, for example cows or humans.
keyPoints: Viviparous give birth to young ones
questions.explanation: They differ in where the young develop.

questions.q: Millions of sperms are released in humans, though only one sperm fertilises an egg. Why?
options: The egg needs many sperms to grow
Many sperms are lost or die on the way, so a large number increases the chance of fertilisation
The body cannot stop producing them
questions.explanation: Only a few of the many sperms reach the egg.

questions.q: Which statement about asexual reproduction is correct?
options: It needs both male and female gametes
The offspring look very different from the parent
questions.explanation: In asexual reproduction a single parent gives rise to offspring, as in Hydra and Amoeba.

questions.q: Describe how a fertilised egg develops into a baby in humans.
questions.answer: The zygote divides repeatedly to form an embryo, which gets attached to the wall of the uterus. The embryo develops body parts, and after the stage called foetus the baby is born after about nine months.
keyPoints: Foetus develops and baby is born
questions.explanation: Development takes place in the uterus.

questions.q: Which of the following is a change in girls during puberty?
questions.explanation: The development of breasts is a change seen in girls at puberty.

questions.q: The thyroid gland is located in the:
questions.explanation: The thyroid gland lies in the neck.

questions.q: Insulin is produced by the:
questions.explanation: The pancreas produces insulin, which controls the sugar level in blood.

questions.q: What is the difference between primary and secondary sexual characters?
questions.answer: Primary sexual characters are the sex organs present from birth, such as testes and ovaries. Secondary sexual characters appear at puberty, such as a beard in boys and development of breasts in girls.
keyPoints: Primary: sex organs present from birth
questions.explanation: Secondary characters develop under the influence of hormones.

questions.q: Why is the use of iodised salt recommended?
options: Iodine in it is needed by the thyroid to make thyroxine and prevents goitre
questions.explanation: Thyroxine needs iodine, so a shortage of iodine causes goitre.

questions.q: Rahul feels moody and irritable during adolescence. What is the most likely explanation?
options: Hormonal changes in the body at this age can affect mood
He is ill with a serious infection
He has a vitamin deficiency only
He has a defect in his eyes
questions.explanation: Mood swings are common during adolescence due to hormonal changes.

questions.q: Why is personal hygiene especially important during adolescence?
questions.answer: At puberty the sweat glands become more active and the skin becomes oily, which can cause body odour and pimples. Bathing daily, wearing clean clothes and keeping the skin clean prevent infections.
questions.explanation: Good hygiene keeps adolescents healthy.

questions.q: Which of the following is a type of friction?
questions.explanation: Static, sliding and rolling are the types of friction.

questions.q: The unit of pressure is the:
questions.explanation: Pressure is measured in pascals (Pa), where 1 Pa is 1 N per square metre.

questions.q: The pressure of the atmosphere acts:
questions.explanation: Air presses on objects from all sides.

questions.q: Why do deep-sea divers wear special suits?
questions.answer: Pressure in water increases with depth, so at great depth the pressure on the body is very large. A special suit protects the diver from this high pressure.
keyPoints: Very high pressure at great depth
questions.explanation: Liquid pressure rises with depth.

questions.q: When you drink through a straw, the liquid rises because:
options: The liquid is lighter than air
Pressure inside the mouth is reduced, and atmospheric pressure pushes the liquid up
questions.explanation: Sucking lowers pressure in the straw, and the higher atmospheric pressure on the liquid pushes it up.

questions.q: It is easier to move a heavy load on a cart with wheels than to drag it on the ground because:
options: Rolling friction is much less than sliding friction
questions.explanation: Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.

questions.q: Why do we sprinkle fine powder on a carrom board before playing?
questions.answer: The powder forms a thin layer between the board and the striker or coins, which reduces friction. The pieces then slide easily and smoothly over the board.
questions.explanation: Powders and oils act as lubricants.

questions.q: In the human ear, which part starts vibrating when sound waves strike it?
questions.explanation: The eardrum is a thin stretched membrane that vibrates when sound waves reach it.

questions.q: Sound cannot travel through:
questions.explanation: Sound needs a medium, and a vacuum is empty.

questions.q: Sounds of frequency higher than 20,000 Hz are called:
questions.explanation: Ultrasonic sounds are above the audible range of humans.

questions.q: Distinguish between music and noise.
questions.answer: Music is a pleasant sound produced by vibrations that are regular and well arranged. Noise is an unpleasant sound with irregular vibrations.
questions.explanation: What is pleasant depends on the type of vibration.

questions.q: A ruler is held on a table with part of it hanging over the edge and plucked. If more of the ruler is slid out over the edge, the sound will have:
questions.explanation: A longer vibrating part vibrates more slowly, so the frequency and pitch are lower.

questions.q: A person who puts an ear on a railway track can hear an approaching train before it can be heard through air. This is because:
options: Sound travels faster in solids than in air
The train makes more sound on the track
questions.explanation: Sound travels faster in a solid such as steel than in air.

questions.q: Describe the path of sound through the human ear in simple steps.
questions.answer: Sound waves enter the ear canal from the pinna and make the eardrum vibrate. The vibrations are passed on through the middle ear to the inner ear, and nerves carry the message to the brain.
keyPoints: Sound enters through pinna and ear canal
Nerves carry signals to the brain
questions.explanation: The ear converts vibrations to nerve signals.

questions.q: Which of the following does NOT conduct electricity?
questions.explanation: Distilled water has no dissolved salts, so it does not conduct. Tap water contains salts and does.

questions.q: Materials through which electric current can pass are called:
questions.explanation: Conductors allow current to flow through them.

questions.q: In copper plating, a solution of copper sulphate is used because it:
options: Provides copper that is deposited on the object
questions.explanation: Copper from the solution is deposited on the article to be plated.

questions.q: When current is passed through acidified water, more bubbles are seen at the negative electrode. The gas there is:
questions.explanation: Water splits into hydrogen and oxygen, and hydrogen is released at the negative electrode.

questions.q: Give two uses of electroplating.
questions.answer: Electroplating is used to give a shiny, attractive finish to objects such as jewellery and car parts. It is also used to protect metals like iron from rusting, for example by chromium or tin plating.
questions.explanation: A thin coat of metal changes the surface of an object.

questions.q: A tester bulb does not glow when its ends are dipped in a liquid. Which conclusion is the most reasonable?
options: The liquid is a very strong conductor
The liquid may be a poor conductor, and a more sensitive LED tester can be tried
questions.explanation: A weak current may be too small to light a bulb but can light an LED.

questions.q: Testing a liquid using a cell is safe, but testing it with the household mains supply is dangerous because:
options: A cell has a low voltage, whereas the mains has a high voltage that can give a serious shock
questions.explanation: The voltage of a cell is low and safe, but mains voltage can be fatal.

questions.q: Why does salt solution conduct electricity while pure distilled water and sugar solution do not?
questions.answer: Salt dissolves in water to give charged particles that can carry the current through the liquid. Distilled water and sugar solution have no such charged particles, so they do not conduct.
keyPoints: Distilled water and sugar solution lack them
questions.explanation: A liquid conducts only if it has charged particles that are free to move.

questions.q: An object becomes electrically charged when:
options: It is rubbed with another suitable object
questions.explanation: Rubbing two different objects together can transfer charge and charge them.

questions.q: The Earth's crust is made of broken parts called:
questions.explanation: The Earth's outermost layer is divided into moving plates, and their movements cause earthquakes.

questions.q: A girl stands 2 m in front of a plane mirror. Her image appears at a distance of how much behind the mirror?
questions.explanation: The image in a plane mirror is as far behind the mirror as the object is in front.

questions.q: A kaleidoscope produces beautiful patterns because of:
questions.explanation: Mirrors inclined at an angle give many images by repeated reflection.

questions.q: How does a periscope help us to see over an obstacle?
questions.answer: A periscope has two plane mirrors fixed at 45 degrees at its two ends. Light from the object reflects from the top mirror to the lower mirror and then to the eye, so we can see objects over a wall.
keyPoints: Two plane mirrors at the ends
questions.explanation: Periscopes use the reflection of light.

questions.q: When white light passes through a prism, which colour bends the most?
questions.explanation: Violet bends the most and red the least, so the colours spread out.

questions.q: A disc painted with the seven rainbow colours is spun very fast. It appears:
questions.explanation: The colours blend in the eye and the disc appears nearly white (Newton's disc).

questions.q: We can see our image in a plane mirror but cannot catch it on a screen. Why?
questions.answer: The image in a plane mirror is virtual. It is formed behind the mirror where light rays only appear to meet, so it cannot be obtained on a screen.
questions.explanation: Real images can be caught on a screen, but virtual ones cannot.
